note: DEC-741 (W4.3): what three 0.170->0.186, Vite 6->8 and React 18->19 cost. Four bench runs, all on this machine inside one session, two at the W4.2 merge commit (6f48471) before any version change and two at the migrated head. Not a new baseline for the product -- baseline-2026-09-05.json remains that -- but the before/after pair the migration is judged on.

comparisonBasis.primary: Isolation. `before` is commit 6f48471 (the W4.2 de-React merge) with its committed lockfile; `after` is the same tree with only the three version bumps and the four source changes they forced. Same machine, same session, same dataset, same bench invocation. This is the only pairing that answers the question the leg asks -- 'did r186/Vite 8/React 19 cost us anything' -- because nothing else differs between the two columns.
comparisonBasis.whyNotTheStatedBasis: The issue names the W1.1/W2.1 pre-migration numbers (baseline-2026-09-05.json) as the comparison. That delta is not attributable to this leg and is not used as one here, for three independent reasons. (1) W4.1 (DEC-739, platform layer and quality ladder) and W4.2 (DEC-740, de-React) both merged in between, so any difference carries their cost as well as the bumps'. (2) The dataset moved: the 2026-09-05 baseline ran `production` at 28,587 stars and 87 planes, and `scale` today is a different fixture at 30,000 stars and 88 planes. (3) The display is different -- see displayCaveat. The 2026-09-05 file is still quoted below as context, but as context and not as a delta.
comparisonBasis.displayCaveat: The reference machine ran at 60 Hz for this session, not the 120 Hz ProMotion the 2026-09-05 baseline recorded. Both vsync runs below therefore sit on a 16.7 ms floor where the baseline sat on an 8.3 ms one, and the vsync column reports `target missed` purely because 17.4 ms p95 exceeds a 16.7 ms target that the panel itself makes unreachable. No vsync number here is comparable with the 2026-09-05 file, in either direction. The uncapped runs are unaffected and are the instrument this leg is read on: with vsync on, a panel reports its own refresh interval whether the frame cost 2 ms or 8.
comparisonBasis.notMeasured: The Iris Xe and 780M field runs stay owner-side (review §9, W0.1); none had arrived by this run. Windows is untested here -- `pnpm windows-kit` is what covers it.

uncapped.role: The load-bearing comparison. Frame rate unlocked, so the number is frame cost and not refresh interval.
uncapped.delta: p95 unchanged at 2.9 ms; p50 unchanged at 2.2 ms; mean fps +6.7 (+1.0%), which is inside this bench's run-to-run spread and is not claimed as an improvement. Verdict: no measurable steady-state cost.
uncapped.maxFrame: 371.6 -> 364.8 ms. Both are DEC-645, unchanged in kind: three.js's WebGLProgram.onFirstUse calls gl.getProgramInfoLog() the first time a newly linked program draws, which is a synchronous round trip that cannot answer until the command buffer drains. It appears only uncapped, at ~680 fps, where the queue is hundreds of frames deep. r186 did not remove it and did not make it worse.

vsync.role: The protocol run PRD 7.2 is judged on -- but see displayCaveat: on a 60 Hz panel it measures the panel.
vsync.delta: p95 17.6 -> 17.4 ms. Both sit on the 60 Hz floor; the difference is scheduling noise, not headroom. Both report PRD 7.2's ceiling (50 fps, p95 <= 33 ms) MET and its target (60 fps, p95 <= 16.7 ms) missed-by-the-display.

servedBytes.status: The evidence bar asks for served bytes rather than local brotli. That cannot be satisfied from this branch, and the gap is real rather than pedantic.
servedBytes.why: check-budget.mjs has no served-bytes mode -- it is brotliCompressSync at quality 11 over local files, with only --dataset and --dist. It models the edge and prints 'encoded transferred size', but never measures it.
servedBytes.whyNotOnThisBranch: A Vercel preview deployment for this branch does exist (PR #49 builds one), so the obstacle is not the absence of a deployment. It is that the preview sits behind Vercel's deployment protection: https://eternities-mtg-app-git-dec741-modernise-diopires-projects.vercel.app/ answers 302 to vercel.com/sso-api. Measuring the migrated build as served needs a protection-bypass token, which is the owner's to issue. That is the concrete unblock -- not 'merge it first'.
servedBytes.measuredOnProduction: Measured against https://eternities-mtg-app.vercel.app on 2026-09-14, which serves the same dataset hash (dabe2c9a68b4d799) the local gate scores, so the two are directly comparable: search.json 227,954 B + sets.bin 513,644 B = 741,598 B = 724.2 KB served with content-encoding: br.
servedBytes.finding: The search-pair row is 724.2 KB as served against a 700.0 KB target -- over it -- while the repo gate reports 669.0 KB and calls it 96% of target. The edge does not reach quality 11, so local brotli under-reports by 55.2 KB on this row. This is a pre-existing measurement gap, not something this leg introduced; the row is data and did not move. Flagged rather than fixed, because re-basing the budget is review amendment B4's open decision and not this leg's to settle.
